title: Learn From Results & Improve the Process
summary: Complete the problem-solving cycle by reviewing results, identifying what was learned, and improving the process for future decisions.
objectives: Compare expected results with actual results.
Identify lessons learned without rewriting past facts.
Recommend process improvements based on evidence.

vocab.def: The result that actually occurred after an action or decision.
A useful conclusion drawn from reviewing what happened and why it matters for future work.
An action intended to address a known problem or reduce the chance of recurrence.
The ongoing practice of using results and feedback to make work more effective over time.

sections.heading: Compare expected and actual results
sections.body: A review begins by comparing what the team expected to happen with what actually happened. Differences can reveal incorrect assumptions, incomplete information, execution problems, or new conditions.

sections.heading: Do not rewrite the history
sections.body: Learning requires an accurate record of the original decision, assumptions, and evidence. Knowing the outcome later should not be used to pretend the answer was obvious earlier.

sections.heading: Look for process improvements
sections.body: The goal is not only to fix one problem. Teams can also improve how they collect information, communicate, make decisions, document reasoning, or verify results.

sections.heading: Improvement should be evidence-based
sections.body: A useful improvement connects to something observed in the results. Changes should address a real weakness rather than create unnecessary complexity.

practice.prompt: A decision solved the immediate problem but created unexpected delays elsewhere. What should the team do with that information?
practice.answer: Include the downstream delay in the review and use it to improve future decision criteria or planning.

practice.prompt: A solution failed because an assumption turned out to be wrong. What is the useful lesson?
practice.answer: Identify how the assumption was made and whether future decisions need better verification before acting.

quiz.question: What is the main purpose of reviewing a workplace decision after implementation?
options: Learn from the actual result and improve future decisions
Prove that the original decision maker was correct
Assign blame for every unexpected outcome
quiz.answer: Learn from the actual result and improve future decisions

lab.objective: Complete an after-action review of a simulated workplace decision by comparing expected and actual results, identifying lessons learned, and proposing one evidence-based improvement.

reflectionPrompt: How can a decision that did not work as expected still produce something valuable?
